title: Italian Africa
capsule: Italian Africa collectively designates the colonial territories Italy assembled in Africa between 1882 and 1943, comprising Eritrea (formally 1890), Italian Somaliland (1889/1905), Libya (conquered 1911–12), and Ethiopia (seized 1935–36 and proclaimed Italian East Africa in 1936 with Victor Emmanuel III as emperor). The conquest of Ethiopia under Marshal Pietro Badoglio, completed by May 1936, briefly gave Italy the largest contiguous colonial block in Africa, with roughly 165,000 settlers in East Africa and 120,000–150,000 in Libya by 1939. British and Commonwealth forces systematically eliminated all Italian East African territories by November 1941, and Libya was lost during the North Africa campaigns by 1943; Italy formally renounced all colonial claims in the 1947 peace treaty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Boundaries of formal colonial administration are well-documented from Italian and British administrative records; the composite geometry aggregating all Italian African territories into one polygon is editorially constructed and somewhat imprecise for the pre-1936 period when holdings were geographically discontinuous.
